title: Observability trace/metrics/log ingestion - debugging breadcrumbs (Eli)
content:
Context:
- Intermittent metric drops seen in prod starting Feb 16. Traces/jaeger sampling looks fine for many services but we see trace ingestion gaps for request-id prefix `svc-a-*` between 03:10-03:18 UTC on 2025-02-17.
- Logs for same window show partial ingestion (log lines present in forwarding layer but absent in central ES index).
- Hypothesis: recent Sidecar change to batching/flush logic (PR #89) + new k8s node taint/eviction pattern caused temporary connector restart and partial offset commit.

What I tried so far (commands & quick results):
- Checked forwarder pod restarts: kubectl -n observability get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
  - result: forwarder-connector-2 restarted at 2025-02-17T03:12:04Z (OOMKilled)

- Inspect forwarder logs around restart:
  $ kubectl -n observability logs forwarder-connector-2 -c forwarder --since=20m | sed -n '1,200p'
  - error snippet: "WARN flusher.go:87: flush failed: write to s3 failed: connection reset by peer"
  - later: "INFO connector.go:210: committing offsets up to 74213" then immediate crash OOMKilled

- Check kafka consumer lag at time of event:
  $ kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group obs-forwarder
  - showed small lag spike (~12k messages) then commit to 0 after restart (possible double commit)

- Checked ES ingestion pipeline for missing trace docs: search by request-id prefix
  $ curl -s "https://es.prod/_search?q=request_id:svc-a-*+@timestamp:[2025-02-17T03:10:00Z TO 2025-02-17T03:20:00Z]" | jq '.hits.total'
  - returned ~1800 docs vs expected ~12k

- Cross-check S3 staging bucket (forwarder writes to s3 before bulk load):
  $ aws s3 ls s3://obs-staging/2025/02/17/03/ --recursive | grep svc-a | wc -l
  - result: 11 objects (size total ~120MB) - suggests not all batches flushed.

- Checked sidecar batching config (configmap obs-forwarder-config):
  batch_size: 5000
  flush_interval_ms: 15000
  max_buffer_bytes: 50MB
  enable_prefetch: true
  (PR #89 changed max_buffer_bytes from 200MB -> 50MB)

Immediate hypotheses:
1) Lowered max_buffer_bytes caused earlier flushes under memory pressure -> more frequent write attempts -> transient S3/connect failures + OOM on connector process leading to partial commits.
2) Connector OOM causes offsets to be committed after partial upload (commit in local state) leading to data loss for the window.
3) Node-level eviction (taint) triggered restarts overlapping with flush operations and S3 transient errors.

Short-term mitigation attempted:
- Rolled forwarder-config to previous values on one staging cluster (max_buffer_bytes: 200MB) -> re-run smoke ingest test for svc-a synthetic workload; result: no drop for 1h test window.
- Temporarily increased forwarder deployment replicas from 3 -> 5 (to spread load) in prod as emergency (monitoring shows reduced per-pod memory high-water).

Next investigative steps (todo):
- Reproduce locally: run forwarder connector with memory cgroup set to lower limit and inject S3 transient disconnects (using toxiproxy). Capture behavior.
- Add additional logging around commit/flush timestamps (connector.go lines around commit) to identify commit-after-failure pattern.
- Audit PR #89 change: why max_buffer_bytes lowered? Was it to avoid memory spikes for specific tenant? Related ticket: JIRA-OBS-5099.
- Check node events around restart time: kubectl describe node <node> and check kubelet eviction logs.
- Confirm Kafka consumer group behavior on crash: do we commit offsets before or after S3 upload? Need to verify commit order in code (consumer_commit.go).
- Add temporary metric/alert: forwarder.flush_error_rate > 0.05 over 5m -> notify #oncall and pause canary (automated rollback flag).

Notes / breadcrumbs for follow-ups:
- Slack convo: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C03OBS1/p1634059200000 (thread with Maya) - she saw similar small drops last month but ignored (might be signal).
- Observed that traces were sampled at different rates across services; sampling mismatch can mask missing spans but not metrics/logs.
- Related: ES bulk index API occasionally returns 413 for oversized bulk (we reduced batch_size? but batch_size still 5000). Need to correlate bulk sizes in S3 objects with ES 413 responses.

Quick patches to propose (if confirmed):
- Revert max_buffer_bytes to 200MB and deploy to prod (canary 10% -> monitor).
- Add robust retry/backoff for S3 writes and ensure commit only after durable upload confirmation.
- Add a short-lived job to reindex objects in S3 for the missing window (if objects exist) into ES.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did connector commit offsets before finishing S3 write? Is commit triggered by internal consumer poll loop independent of S3 success?
- Did Kafka consumer group config enable "auto.commit"? (I think we've turned it off historically but need to check).
- Are there other forwarder deployments with same config change that haven't been rolled back? (search: kustomize overlays)

Action log (who to ping):
- @Maya for S3 object scan and attempt reindex of present objects.
- @Jon to review consumer commit logic in codebase (consumer_commit.go).
- @Infra on node eviction events and kubelet logs.

If I don't follow up within 24h: escalate to oncall and open hotfix PR to revert config change.

Misc quick snippets saved:
- Connector panic trace (short): "panic: runtime: out of memory
 goroutine 1 [running]:
 runtime.throw(0x... )
 ..."
- Kafka describe output sample: "GROUP: obs-forwarder PARTITIONS: topic=obs-topic-001 partition=12 current-offset=74213 log-end-offset=74213 lag=0 owner=forwarder-connector-1"

End of notes.
